title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1966-11-19
lineage: Master Reel -> Dat -> CD -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> FLAC (1 Disc Audio / 1 Disc FLAC)

ai_review.summary: Stunning 1966 soundboard capture with blazing Pigpen performances and crystal‑clear mix
ai_review.review: The November 19, 1966 recording is hailed as a rare early‑Dead gem – the Miller transfer delivers an unusually crisp stereo hi‑fi sound for its era, letting the raw power of Pigpen’s vocals and organ shine through.  The show bursts with energy, highlighted by “Hi‑Heel Sneakers,” “Cream Puff War,” “Pain In My Heart,” and an all‑Pigpen second set that many reviewers call the best example of the band’s early blues‑rock period.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen detailed, mostly 5‑star reviews praise both the performance and the audio quality; only minor technical quibbles (channel swap, speed correction, a cut in “Dancin’”) keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Stereo hi‑fi mix praised as crystal clear; Miller’s transfer noted for superb clarity.  A few users mention channel reversal and a +2 % pitch correction needed, but overall the audio is considered outstanding for a 1966 source.

standout_songs: Pain In My Heart (Otis Redding cover)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Two‑set structure with a blues‑heavy first set and an all‑Pigpen second set; flow is praised for its raw, early‑Dead energy despite a noted abrupt cut during “Dancin’ In The Street.”

band_member_comments.Pigpen: Dominates the performance; his vocals and organ on “Same Thing,” “Pain In My Heart,” and other blues numbers are repeatedly highlighted as spectacular.
